Personality: Theodotos the Aetolian, a prominent figure of the Theodotidai, Proud, martial, inspired by the glorious legacy of Alexander the Great; master of sarissa phalanx doctrine and companion cavalry shock tactics. Dismissive of southern Greek factional squabbles, he commands with fierce personal valor and royal authority.
Background: Theodotos the Aetolian owes allegiance to the Seleucid Empire, hailing from the noble house of Theodotidai. Historical Record: Ptolemy's governor of Coele-Syria, who held it against Antiochus in 221 BC, then, despised at the Alexandrian court, went over to him in 219 BC with Tyre and Ptolemais. Bold to the point of folly, he means to settle the war at a stroke by stealing into the Egyptian camp and killing Ptolemy himself. Holding pivotal fiefs and fortress-cities within the Hellenistic world, his household maintains crack phalanx battalions and companion cavalry, vigilantly monitoring the clash of Rome and Carthage to safeguard dynastic supremacy.
